name: AI Data-Centre Liquid Cooling: Fluids, Hoses & Heat Exchangers
scope: Indian listed suppliers of coolants/dielectric fluids, liquid-cooling skids and hoses, and heat exchangers/cooling systems for AI data centres, and how much of the theme is already priced in.

summary.one_line: Aeroflex (skids) and KRN (heat exchangers) are still the only Indian listed names with quantified data-centre cooling revenue. The fluids leg has products but no disclosed sales, and it has already re-rated on transformer-oil earnings. This week the theme cooled: over the past month KRN is down 13%, Aeroflex 7%, and Savita is 11% below its 30 Sep record.
key_points: IndexBox forecasts an 18.5% CAGR for direct-to-chip liquid cooling over 2026-2035 (baseline 12.0%), and 15.2% for immersion-cooling fluids. It puts the practical limit of air cooling at 30-50 kW per rack, against AI racks above 100 kW (S1, S2).

JLL puts India's data-centre capacity at 1.6 GW in mid-2026 and expects 6 GW by 2029. H1 2026 absorption was 101 MW, 82% of it pre-committed hyperscale capacity. JLL says USD 110 bn of investment is needed by 2029 (S3).

Aeroflex sold Rs 32.4 cr of liquid-cooling SFN skids in Q1 FY27, about 23% of revenue. Skid capacity is 9,000 units a year, targeted at 15,000 by Q3 FY27, with Rs 102 cr of capex budgeted for skids and hoses (S7).
Data centres were about 16% of KRN's FY26 revenue (18.7% in Q4), and Vertiv's quality audit has been approved. FY26 operating cash flow was -Rs 113.80 cr (S10).

Savita (QuantiCool PG 25 coolant for direct liquid cooling) and Apar (Poweroil DC 10 immersion fluid) have data-centre products but disclose no revenue from them. Their re-rating rests on transformer-oil margins, which Apar partly attributes to inventory gains (S9, S12, S13, S14, S15).

Blue Star took about Rs 1,500 cr of data-centre MEP orders in Q1 FY27 and targets about Rs 4,000 cr of data-centre MEP revenue by FY29. Its Q1 FY27 call did not mention liquid cooling, and it has a 10-12% share in data-centre chillers (S16).
Not every hyperscale build is going liquid. Google says its USD 15 bn Visakhapatnam campus will use advanced air cooling to protect local water, and the project faces litigation (S24).
Added this week: BPCL, a large cap, co-developed an Indian data-centre liquid coolant with Refroid and plans to use it in its own data centres first, with no sales disclosed (S25).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Aeroflex: skids earn 22-26% EBITDA margins against 16-20% for hoses, and capacity is rising from 9,000 to 15,000 units (S7).
KRN: Vertiv's audit is approved, with prototype and then mass production to follow drawing approvals. Plant II utilisation is guided to about 50% in FY27 and about 80% the year after (S10).
Blue Star: guides to about Rs 3,000 cr of data-centre MEP inflow in FY27 and about Rs 4,500 cr in FY28. Its June 2026 MEP order book was above Rs 7,700 cr (S16).
Fluids makers (Savita, Apar, Castrol, BPCL) have coolants ready or in trials. That is an option not yet visible in their reported numbers (S9, S14, S17, S25).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Aeroflex's liquid-cooling orders so far (about Rs 16 cr in two orders by Oct 2025) come from one US-listed client's Indian data centre. It also faces a Rs 41.76 cr tax demand for AY2018-19, which it is appealing (S5, S6).
KRN's working capital is stretched: FY26 operating cash flow was -Rs 113.80 cr, inventories Rs 272.91 cr and current borrowings Rs 187.10 cr (S10).
Apar says Q1 FY27 oil margins included inventory gains that reverse when gas-oil prices fall, and the same commodity sensitivity applies to Savita (S15).

Air cooling is still being chosen for some Indian hyperscale sites, for example Google in Visakhapatnam (S24). Local CDU makers such as KühlTherm are adding capacity that competes with component suppliers (S19).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: Q2 FY27 results (late Oct to Nov 2026): Aeroflex's skid revenue share, which was 23% in Q1, and KRN's data-centre mix, which was 18.7% in Q4 FY26 (S7, S10).
Whether Aeroflex discloses a second liquid-cooling customer (S5).
First disclosed data-centre fluid revenue at Savita, Apar, Castrol or BPCL (S12, S15, S17, S25).
JLL's next half-yearly update on progress toward 6 GW by 2029, and hyperscalers' cooling choices (S3, S24).

sections.title: Theme explainer: why AI is forcing liquid cooling

blocks.text: Liquid cooling removes heat with a fluid instead of air. In direct-to-chip (DTC) systems, a coolant, typically a propylene-glycol/water mix such as Savita's 25% PG product, runs through cold plates on the processors (S9). Coolant distribution units (CDUs), manifolds, skids and hoses circulate it, and heat exchangers pass the heat on to facility water. In immersion cooling, servers sit in a dielectric (non-conductive) fluid such as Apar's Poweroil DC 10 (S14). IndexBox's direct-to-chip report says air cooling hits its physical limits above 30 kW per rack and stops being viable for hyperscalers above 50 kW, while AI/ML racks exceed 100 kW (S1). Netweb says its joint DTC work with Vertiv aims to cross 200 kW of IT load per rack (S18).

blocks.caption: Liquid-cooling forecasts (the forecasters' figures, not ours)
rows: Baseline 12.0% CAGR, but the page gives a baseline index of ~420, which implies about 15%

blocks.text: IndexBox puts data-centre cooling at 45% of immersion-fluid demand in 2026. The rest comes from EV batteries (20%), HPC (15%), power transformers (10%) and crypto mining (10%) (S2). So Indian fluids makers can fill their ester and glycol plants with transformer and EV demand even if data-centre orders are slow to come.

Correction this week: last edition dated the IndexBox direct-to-chip article 1 Oct 2026. The article is dated 23 Sep 2026, and 1 Oct is the report-update date. The page's 12.0% baseline CAGR and its ~420 baseline index do not reconcile (S1).

sections.title: India build-out, capex and local content

blocks.text: JLL's mid-year report (31 Aug 2026) estimates India's capacity at 1.6 GW in mid-2026 and expects it to triple to 6 GW by 2029. H1 2026 absorption was 101 MW, 82% of it pre-committed hyperscale capacity, and new supply was 85 MW. JLL counts more than USD 50 bn of hyperscaler commitments and says USD 110 bn of investment is needed by 2029. It lists liquid, direct-to-chip and immersion cooling among the green practices being adopted (S3). Cooling choices are not uniform, though: Google says its USD 15 bn Visakhapatnam campus will use advanced air cooling to protect local water resources. Activists have challenged the project in the Andhra Pradesh High Court over water stress (S24).

blocks.title: India data-centre capacity (JLL)
blocks.source: Source: JLL India Data Centre 2026 Mid-Year Report (S3)

blocks.text: We still have no accessible source that splits India's cooling spend between liquid and air over the next 3-5 years, so we give no estimate. Google's choice of air cooling at Visakhapatnam (S24) is a reminder that the liquid share will vary by site, water availability and rack density.

items: CDUs and rear-door heat exchangers: the unlisted Ahmedabad start-up KühlTherm launched Indian-made CDUs and RDHx units in Aug 2026. It has 300 MW of capacity and targets 2 GW by 2027 (S19). We found no Indian listed CDU or cold-plate maker.
Racks and servers: Netweb and Vertiv both design, engineer and manufacture in India, and Vertiv supplies CDUs and free-cooling chillers for Netweb's rack-scale systems (S18).
Skids and hoses: Aeroflex makes SFN skid assemblies in India and is expanding flexible-hose capacity from 17.5 to 20.0 mn metres a year (S7).
Heat exchangers: KRN's new Plant II ran at about 15% utilisation in FY26 (S10).

Fluids: Savita's Phase 2 synthetic-ester plant was commissioned on 28 Feb 2026 (S11), and it sells QuantiCool glycol coolants for direct liquid cooling (S9). Apar markets Poweroil DC 10 (S14). Castrol says its coolants are ready for India and in tests with OEMs (S17). BPCL co-developed an Indian data-centre coolant with Refroid (S25).

subsections.title: Flow components and heat exchangers (quantified exposure)

blocks.text: On 18 Dec 2025, Aeroflex's board approved Rs 97.56 cr of capex to raise skid capacity to 15,000 units a year, funded by Rs 42.56 cr of internal accruals and a Rs 55 cr preferential issue (S4). ICICI Direct's Q2 FY26 note records two liquid-cooling orders of about Rs 16 cr in total from a US client, including a Rs 7.8 cr follow-on for the client's Indian data centre, and an agreement to supply as that client builds Indian capacity (S5). In Q1 FY27, total income rose 72.4% to Rs 145.97 cr, PAT rose 162% to Rs 18.79 cr and EBITDA margin was 23.04%. Skids contributed Rs 32.4 cr, and capex is now Rs 102 cr, of which Rs 48 cr is for skids and Rs 54 cr for hoses (S7).

Data centres were about 16% of KRN's FY26 consolidated revenue of Rs 600.06 cr, and 18.7% in Q4. Vertiv's quality-audit approval is complete, and prototype and mass production follow drawing approvals (S10). Blue Star's data-centre exposure is MEP projects and chillers, not disclosed liquid-cooling hardware. It took about Rs 1,500 cr of data-centre MEP orders in Q1 FY27 and targets data-centre MEP revenue of about Rs 4,000 cr, close to 20% of the total, by FY29. In chillers, its data-centre share is 10-12% against four or five multinationals (S16).

subsections.title: Fluids leg: products ready, revenue undisclosed

blocks.text: Savita's data-centre page lists QuantiCool PG 25, a propylene-glycol coolant 'designed exclusively' for direct liquid cooling, plus a QuantiCool DLC grade. It names no immersion dielectric, customers or revenue (S9). Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 49.6% to Rs 1,479.76 cr and PAT to Rs 292.25 cr, with no data-centre disclosure (S12). Apar's oils EBITDA rose 214.2% to Rs 329 cr in Q1 FY27. Its data-centre progress is in US cables (approvals for contractors serving Meta, Microsoft and Google), and the coverage does not mention fluids (S15). Castrol India says data-centre cooling is not yet material because announced projects are not yet consuming fluid (S17). BPCL's coolant, developed with Refroid, is to be shown first in BPCL's own data centres, with no volumes disclosed (S25).

Coverage by size: the two small caps, Aeroflex and KRN, are the only names reporting quantified data-centre cooling revenue (S7, S10). Savita (small cap), Castrol, Blue Star and Netweb (mid caps), and Apar and BPCL (large caps) have products or adjacencies but no disclosed data-centre cooling revenue. We found no Indian listed CDU or cold-plate maker; the domestic CDU makers we found, such as KühlTherm, are unlisted (S19). That gap reflects how early the niche is.

blocks.title: 6-month share-price return to 12 Oct 2026
blocks.source: Source: Anand Rathi quote pages (S8, S20, S21, S22, S23)

items: Savita closed at Rs 763.95, about 11.5% below its 52-week high of Rs 862.80 (S20). Coverage of its record high on 30 Sep credited transformer oils, not data-centre coolants (S13).
Aeroflex trades about 11% below its 52-week high of Rs 583.70 (S8). KRN is 17% below its high of Rs 1,676.25 (S21). Both rose sharply on the liquid-cooling story and fell over the past month.

Broker coverage is thin. ICICI Direct publishes result updates on Aeroflex (S5). Otherwise, coverage is mostly retail and fintech media such as Trade Brains, DSIJ, ScanX, Whalesbook and Multibagg (S7, S10, S13, S15, S17).

blocks.text: The Anand Rathi pages are internally inconsistent: each page's narrative text and FAQ give different return and P/E figures from its own table. Savita's P/E is shown as 12.26 in the table and 15.03 in the FAQ (S20). Treat the returns as indicative; the dashboard shows live numbers.

items: Single-customer dependence: Aeroflex's disclosed liquid-cooling orders come from one US client's Indian data centre (S5). Last edition's 'India-exclusive' wording could not be re-confirmed this week because the transcript page now returns an error, so we have dropped it.

Tax dispute: Aeroflex faces an income-tax demand of Rs 41.76 cr for AY2018-19 (order dated 25 Mar 2026) over disallowed interest-waiver claims on working-capital loans. It is appealing and says it expects no material impact (S6).
Working capital: KRN's FY26 operating cash flow was -Rs 113.80 cr, compared with +Rs 21.44 cr in FY25 (S10).
Margin reversal in fluids: Apar booked about Rs 93 cr of inventory-valuation provision, and DSIJ says its 19.3% oil margin is unlikely to be a normalised run rate (S15).
Technology choice: hyperscalers may still choose air cooling where water is scarce (S24), and IndexBox lists competition from direct-to-chip as a constraint on immersion fluids (S2).
Competition: global OEMs (Vertiv) and new local CDU makers (KühlTherm, targeting 2 GW by 2027) are localising (S18, S19).

companies.name: Aeroflex Industries Ltd
companies.role: Makes stainless-steel flexible hoses and liquid-cooling SFN skid assemblies, and has supplied skids for a US-listed client's Indian data centre (S5, S7).
companies.impact: Skids were about 23% of Q1 FY27 revenue, with capacity heading to 15,000 units by Q3 FY27. It is the most direct listed exposure, but it depends on one customer and faces a Rs 41.76 cr tax demand. The stock is up 201% over one year but down 7% over one month (S6, S7, S8).

companies.name: KRN Heat Exchanger and Refrigeration Ltd
companies.role: Makes fin-and-tube heat-exchanger coils for HVAC&R, including data-centre cooling, and has Vertiv's quality-audit approval (S10).
companies.impact: Data centres were about 16% of FY26 revenue (18.7% in Q4). Working capital is stretched, and the stock is down 13% over one month (S10, S21).

companies.name: Blue Star Ltd
companies.role: Delivers data-centre MEP projects and chillers, with about a 30% share in data-centre MEP and 10-12% in data-centre chillers (S16).
companies.impact: Data-centre MEP is scaling toward about Rs 4,000 cr of revenue by FY29. No liquid-cooling revenue is disclosed, and the stock is down 17% over one year (S16, S23).

companies.name: Savita Oil Technologies Ltd
companies.role: Sells QuantiCool PG 25 propylene-glycol coolant for direct liquid cooling, and commissioned Phase 2 of its synthetic-ester plant on 28 Feb 2026 (S9, S11).
companies.impact: The stock is up 127% over six months on transformer-oil profits, but is 11.5% off its record high. Data-centre fluid revenue is not disclosed (S12, S13, S20).

companies.name: Apar Industries Ltd
companies.role: Markets Poweroil DC 10, a single-phase immersion dielectric fluid, alongside data-centre cables (S14).
companies.impact: Its data-centre progress is visible in US cable approvals, not fluids. Oil margins include inventory gains that can reverse (S15).

companies.name: Castrol India Ltd
companies.role: Has immersion and direct-to-chip coolants ready for India and in tests with OEMs (S17).
companies.impact: Management calls data-centre cooling not yet material and the tests long-term, so there is no near-term earnings effect (S17).

companies.name: Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd
companies.role: Co-developed, with Refroid Technologies, what it calls India's first indigenous liquid coolant for AI data centres (S25).
companies.impact: Large-cap optionality only: deployment starts in BPCL's own data centres, with no volumes or revenue disclosed (S25).

companies.name: Netweb Technologies India Ltd
companies.role: Indian server OEM building direct-to-chip liquid-cooled GPU systems with Vertiv's CDUs and free-cooling chillers (S18).
companies.impact: A downstream adjacency that pulls through liquid-cooling content rather than making fluids or hardware for it (S18).
